keyframe_review.note: 825-829, 3,490 km2. The Sobrarbe page calls the kingdom 'legendary' ('the legendary predecessor of the Kingdom of Aragon'), places its founding in 724 only as legend (Christians met 'at Espelunga de Galión in the year 724' and elected García Ximéniz) and dates nothing historical in 825-829; the fueros de Sobrarbe are 'claimed to be mostly fabricated'. The cells are those of the County of Aragon (attested 807, Aznar I count 809-820, García the Bad 820-833; County of Aragon page), so the land is drawn as that county. The dossier exists only to answer the Cliopatria row; render nothing for Sobrarbe.

region.text: the cells of Cliopatria's Sobrarbe row, equal to the county of Aragon

ledger.note: 825: Cliopatria begins a 'Kingdom of Sobrarbe' row. The page is silent on 825; it presents the kingdom as a legend founded in 724 (García Ximéniz, 724-758). The same land is the county of Aragon from 807, so no founding is drawn.
829: the Cliopatria row ends and the county of Aragon (the same cells) carries on in 830. No historical event is dated to 829 on the page.

certainty.note: A legendary kingdom; no boundary line exists.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Sobrarbe' (825-829) is a legendary kingdom: the Sobrarbe page presents the founding in 724, the regnal list (García Ximéniz 724-758 to Fortún Garcés II 885-901) and the fueros as legend or fabrication, and the cells equal the County of Aragon's. Recommendation to the orchestrator: drop the row or merge it into county-of-aragon (which starts in 807); the dossier keeps Cliopatria's years 825-829 so the validator and the map stay consistent, with every confidence at 1 and the verdict 'wrong'. No rulers are listed because the list is legendary. The historical county of Sobrarbe appears later: Sancho III of Pamplona expanded into the depopulated former county in 1015 and Gonzalo ruled Sobrarbe and Ribagorza 1035-1045 (the kingdom-of-pamplona and county-of-ribagorza dossiers).
